other_failure_modes.name: transductive_imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Missing values in the test set are imputed using the test set's own medians, rather than statistics learned from the training set. This transductive approach is invalid for production where samples arrive individually.

other_failure_modes.name: transductive_rank_ensembling
other_failure_modes.description: The ensembling strategy uses a rank transformation on the test predictions, making the output for any single test instance dependent on the distribution of the entire test batch. This prevents valid out-of-sample prediction on new, single instances.

other_failure_modes.name: data_leakage_in_cv_imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Imputation is performed on the entire training set before cross-validation splits, leaking validation fold statistics into the training folds during evaluation.

summary: The agent builds a well-structured cross-validated ensemble with thoughtful feature engineering, but critically relies on transductive transformations. By computing medians and prediction ranks directly on the test set, the solution violates out-of-sample prediction principles, rendering the model unsuitable for production use on individual new samples. Additionally, global imputation on the training set prior to CV splits introduces internal data leakage.
